source.citation: Garcia, M. P. C., Paz-Alberto, A. M., Abella, T. A., Sace, C. F., Claudio, E. G., & Gabriel, A. G. (2018). Assessment of the Diversity of Macro Aquatic Species in Amburayan River in Kapangan, Benguet in the Philippines. Open Journal of Marine Science, 8, 323-354. https://doi.org/10.4236/ojms.2018.83018
source.attributionAndChanges: Attribute all six authors, article title, journal, volume, pages, DOI and CC BY 4.0; clearly mark any corrections or derived changes. License on the article does not independently license its separately cited sources.

study.studyWaterbody: Amburayan River, Kapangan, Benguet, Cordillera Administrative Region
study.catchSamplingFrequencyAsReported: Every two days under the described NSAP procedure; the paper does not supply a complete dated observation log.
study.samplingAreaPerStation: Five 10 m by 12 m quadrats (600 m2 per station; 3,000 m2 total across five stations).

stationCoordinateStatements.coordinateRole: Reported head endpoint of the five-station sampling reach; not a coordinate for all Station 1 samples or an independently verified station point.

study.otherLocationStatement: The paper describes an approximately 9,323 m river reach from Atok toward the La Union boundary and says data gathering was concentrated in Barangay Cuba, Kapangan. It does not publish coordinates for each of the five stations or a machine-readable sampling-site dataset.
study.samplingMethods: FGD with ten local fishermen helped select sites; macrofauna were collected using traditional/custom fishing gears and an NSAP-derived catch-monitoring procedure. Identification used references and expert assistance; the paper says some samples were intended for NFRDI DNA barcoding, but later states NFRDI could not accommodate analysis because reagents were unavailable.
dateAndScopeLimits: The source is a historical, localized survey from 2014-2015, not a current inventory or a complete Amburayan watershed checklist.
The main catch survey spans five stations in the Kapangan study area; it should not be projected to all of Benguet, the whole Amburayan River, or downstream La Union.
The article reports 14 macrofauna taxa, not 14 fish species: nine finfish-group entries, four crustacean entries and one gastropod entry. Some entries are genus-only.
The paper gives two reach-end coordinate statements, not per-station coordinates. Do not convert them into station pins, fish locations, or river geometry.

The article describes the fish sampling as every two days, but provides no complete event-level dates or station-by-date matrix. Its seasonal and catch-period narrative is not a present-day season or catchability rule.

sourceReportedTotals.interpretation: These are article-reported historical survey totals, including unresolved/genus-only entries; they are not a current population estimate or complete species count.

dietAndInteractionEvidence.admissionRule: Treat these as claims reported in a historical article only. Verify the underlying references and identify diet method, life stage, season and habitat before any species-food profile. Keep natural-diet evidence separate from angler bait suggestions.

qualityAndLocalityIssues: The paper says nine finfish among 14 macrofauna taxa; some entries are genus-only and one identification remained unresolved after the described NFRDI DNA-analysis request could not proceed because reagents were unavailable.

The source has visible spelling/format errors, including Gambussia/Gambussiaaffinis, Oreochromis nilotocus, joined taxon strings, and inconsistent higher taxonomy. These have not been silently corrected.

It states five stations and reports only Station 1 head-point and Station 5 tail-point coordinates in the summary; no individual station coordinates or machine-readable station file was found in the reviewed article.
The location section describes an approximately 9,323 m river reach, while sampling is concentrated in Barangay Cuba, Kapangan. Do not extend the catch list over the whole reach or into La Union.

The article reports some taxa as community-reported/in-season but explicitly says common carp and African catfish were not caught during the stated December 2014-January 2015 period. Separate fisher reports from collected specimens.
The diet paragraph contains untraceable or mismatched citations and does not describe gut-content sampling. No natural-food profile or bait recommendation is approved from it.
The paper reports introduced tilapia and mosquito fish; this review does not independently validate their regional introduction histories or current status.

disposition.reason: The CC BY 4.0 article is reusable with attribution, but this historical five-station study has unresolved names, limited reach, incomplete per-station coordinates, and weak/citation-conflicted secondary diet claims. This review records source evidence only and does not admit occurrence or diet claims to Bangwit.

nextAction: Independently cross-check the nine fish source labels against a fish taxonomic authority while retaining every verbatim spelling; separately investigate the original voucher/identification certificates and station coordinate map if available. Keep the food-web claims held until their original references and evidence methods are verified.
